1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line spacing, though letter spacing appears standard rather than distinctly generous and no specifically dyslexia-friendly font is evident.

2.why: No italics or all-caps text appear anywhere, and all copy is broken into short lines rather than dense blocks.

3.why: The narrow single-column card layout, large text, full-width inputs and large buttons render clearly at the mobile screen size shown.

4.why: Instructions are brief and plain, e.g. 'Start your security setup.' and 'Get a six-digit identity code for this demo.'

5.why: Expected input is exemplified by the 'name@example.com' email placeholder and the '123456' placeholder in the six-digit code field.

6.why: No step requires reading a long text block; the longest copy (the activity-log description) is optional and not needed to proceed.

7.why: No copy-to-clipboard control is visible, and the identity code is shown only in the browser console, forcing the user to read and retype it.

8.why: No QR code or any equivalent alternative to manual entry appears on any of the five screens.

9.why: The standard labeled email and password fields might work with autofill and password managers, but no such support can be confirmed from the screenshots.

10.why: The heading and the large blue primary button make the step and action stand out, but the segmented progress bar shows the same single filled segment on every screen and has no labels.

11.why: Each screen presents one filled primary button ('Sign in', 'Get identity code', 'Check code'); the re-request option on step 3 is clearly styled as secondary.

12.why: After each action a banner states the outcome and next step, e.g. 'Signed in successfully. Next: get your identity code.'

13.why: The user can retry after an error and re-request the identity code with no penalty shown, but no reveal/hide option for the password or codes is visible.

14.why: The error 'That code does not match. Check the six digits, or request a new code.' states the problem and the fix without blaming the user.

15.why: The screen explicitly states 'There is no reading timer. Take as long as you need.' and no countdown or time limit appears anywhere.
